comparisons.peer_topic: Shareholder Returns and Capital Repurchase Program
comparisons.peer_summary: Citi returned $6.7 billion to shareholders in 2024 via dividends and repurchases, and authorized a new $20 billion multiyear repurchase program in January 2025 with $1.5 billion planned for Q1 2025, subject to regulatory capital uncertainty.
comparisons.comparison:
While BofAS discloses specific broker-dealer net capital metrics (tentative and regulatory net capital in billions of dollars), Citi's related disclosure focuses on shareholder returns and capital repurchases, noting uncertainty regarding regulatory capital requirements as a factor in its $20 billion repurchase program authorization. Unlike BofAS, which quantifies its capital cushion against specific minimums, Citi references the general concept of regulatory capital requirements influencing strategic capital deployment decisions rather than reporting its own net capital balances or minimum requirements.
Target: "BofAS also had regulatory net capital of $21.0 billion, which exceeded the minimum requirement of $4.5 billion."
Peer: "After the first quarter of 2025, Citi will continue to assess the level of common share repurchases on a quarter-by-quarter basis given uncertainty regarding regulatory capital requirements, among other factors."

sentences.text: BofAS also had regulatory net capital of $21.0 billion, which exceeded the minimum requirement of $4.5 billion.

• Citi returned $6.7 billion to common shareholders in the form of dividends ($4.2 billion) and share repurchases ($2.5 billion) in 2024. As previously disclosed, on January 13, 2025, Citigroup's Board of Directors authorized a new, multiyear $20 billion common stock repurchase program, with planned repurchases of $1.5 billion during the first quarter of 2025, subject to market conditions and other factors. After the first quarter of 2025, Citi will continue to assess the level of common share repurchases on a quarter-by-quarter basis given uncertainty regarding regulatory capital requirements, among other factors.

comparisons.peer_topic: GS&Co. Regulatory Capital Framework and Compliance
comparisons.peer_summary: GS&Co. had regulatory net capital of $21.31 billion as of December 2024, exceeding minimum requirements by $15.87 billion, and held tentative net capital in excess of $6 billion, meeting all SEC and CFTC capital and notification requirements.
comparisons.comparison:
Both BofAS and GS&Co. are broker-dealers subject to SEC Rule 15c3-1 Alternative Net Capital Requirements, maintaining tentative net capital in excess of $5 billion and net capital in excess of $1 billion. Both entities are also subject to an SEC notification requirement if tentative net capital falls below $6 billion. BofAS reported tentative net capital of $23.6 billion and regulatory net capital of $21.0 billion, exceeding its specific minimum requirement of $4.5 billion. GS&Co. reported regulatory net capital of $21.31 billion, exceeding minimum requirements by $15.87 billion, and confirmed it held tentative net capital in excess of both the minimum and notification requirements.
Target: "At December 31, 2024, BofAS had tentative net capital of $23.6 billion."; "BofAS also had regulatory net capital of $21.0 billion, which exceeded the minimum requirement of $4.5 billion."
Peer: "GS&Co. had regulatory net capital, as defined by Rule 15c3-1 of the SEC, of $21.31 billion as of December 2024..."; "GS&Co. is also required to notify the SEC in the event that its tentative net capital is less than $6 billion."

sentences.text: At December 31, 2024, BofAS had tentative net capital of $23.6 billion.
BofAS also had regulatory net capital of $21.0 billion, which exceeded the minimum requirement of $4.5 billion.

GS&Co. had regulatory net capital, as defined by Rule 15c3-1 of the SEC, of $21.31 billion as of December 2024 and $20.25 billion as of December 2023, which exceeded the greater of the minimum amounts required under Rule 15c3-1 of the SEC and Rules 1.17 and Part 23 Subpart E of the CFTC by $15.87 billion as of December 2024 and $15.07 billion as of December 2023.
GS&Co. is also required to notify the SEC in the event that its tentative net capital is less than $6 billion.

comparisons.peer_topic: Regulatory capital requirements for J.P. Morgan Securities
comparisons.peer_summary: J.P. Morgan Securities is subject to net capital requirements under the SEC's Net Capital Rule (Rule 15c3-1), has elected to compute minimum net capital using Alternative Net Capital Requirements, and as a registered swap dealer and security-based swap dealer, must maintain tentative net capital above $5.0 billion and notify regulators if it falls below $6.0 billion.
comparisons.comparison:
Both BofAS and J.P. Morgan Securities are subject to the SEC Net Capital Rule (Rule 15c3-1) and have elected the Alternative Net Capital Requirements. Both entities, acting as registered swap dealers, are required to maintain tentative net capital in excess of $5.0 billion. Furthermore, both entities are subject to a notification threshold of $6.0 billion, requiring them to notify regulators if tentative net capital falls below that amount. While the target discloses specific capital balances, J.P. Morgan Securities' disclosure confirms compliance with these structural requirements and states it maintained tentative net capital in excess of these minimum and notification requirements.
Target: "BofAS provides institutional services, and in accordance with the alternative net capital requirements, is required to maintain tentative net capital in excess of $5.0 billion..."; "BofAS must also notify the SEC in the event its tentative net capital is less than $6.0 billion."
Peer: "J.P. Morgan Securities is subject to the regulatory capital requirements of Rule 15c3-1..."; "J.P. Morgan Securities is subject to alternative minimum net capital requirements and required to hold 'tentative net capital' in excess of $5.0 billion."; "J.P. Morgan Securities is also required to notify the SEC and CFTC in the event that its tentative net capital is less than $6.0 billion."

sentences.text: BofAS provides institutional services, and in accordance with the alternative net capital requirements, is required to maintain tentative net capital in excess of $5.0 billion and net capital in excess of the greater of $1.0 billion or a certain percentage of its reserve requirement in addition to a certain percentage of securities-based swap risk margin.
BofAS must also notify the SEC in the event its tentative net capital is less than $6.0 billion.
J.P. Morgan Securities is subject to the regulatory capital requirements of Rule 15c3-1 under the Securities Exchange Act of 1934 (the "Net Capital Rule").

As a result of additional SEC and CFTC capital and financial reporting requirements for security-based swap dealers and swap dealers, J.P. Morgan Securities is subject to alternative minimum net capital requirements and required to hold "tentative net capital" in excess of $5.0 billion.
J.P. Morgan Securities is also required to notify the SEC and CFTC in the event that its tentative net capital is less than $6.0 billion.

comparisons.peer_topic: Minimum Capital and TLAC Ratio Requirements
comparisons.peer_summary: The company is required to maintain minimum risk-based and leverage-based capital and Total Loss-Absorbing Capacity (TLAC) ratios.
comparisons.comparison:
BofAS discloses specific net capital requirements and balances for its broker-dealer subsidiary (BofAS) under SEC and CFTC rules. In contrast, Morgan Stanley's disclosure pertains to the holding company's requirement to maintain minimum risk-based and leverage-based capital and TLAC ratios, which are different regulatory frameworks typically applied to the bank holding company rather than the specific broker-dealer net capital computations described for BofAS, GS, and JPM.
Target: "BofAS provides institutional services, and in accordance with the alternative net capital requirements, is required to maintain tentative net capital in excess of $5.0 billion..."
Peer: "We are required to maintain minimum risk-based and leverage-based capital and TLAC ratios."

sentences.text: BofAS provides institutional services, and in accordance with the alternative net capital requirements, is required to maintain tentative net capital in excess of $5.0 billion and net capital in excess of the greater of $1.0 billion or a certain percentage of its reserve requirement in addition to a certain percentage of securities-based swap risk margin.
We are required to maintain minimum risk-based and leverage-based capital and TLAC ratios.
